clue.text: Otherwise tick and store everything for sale

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters of the three words are set out differently

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper is told to tick off and put away all the goods on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Otherwise' tells you to rearrange TICK AND STORE, all twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader's stock in trade is the whole range of goods kept on hand to sell.

clue.text: Trip and fall under front of steamroller

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece under another is written after it
the front of a word is its opening letter, here taken from steamroller

parts.note: to fall is to tumble

explanation.surface: Someone trips and goes down beneath an approaching steamroller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' gives S from steamroller; 'under' puts TUMBLE below it in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble is to miss one's footing, much as a trip makes one lurch.

clue.text: Man not using his head in card game

indicators.note: not using the head means the opening letter of the word for man is dropped

parts.note: hombre is Spanish for man, used in English slang for a fellow

explanation.surface: A gambler plays cards thoughtlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not using his head' removes the H from HOMBRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre is an old three-handed card game popular in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

clue.text: Edging on flags restrains, say, the general effect

indicators.note: say signals that the word for restrains is to be heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: restrains means curbs
the tone of something is its general character or effect

explanation.surface: A paving border holds the flagstones in place and sets the look of the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns CURBS into its sound-alike KERBS, the British spelling of a pavement edge. Flags here are flagstones, the slabs of a pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerbstone is one of the stones forming the raised border of a pavement of flagstones.

clue.text: Pooter's critical comment on wine

definitions.meaning: Charles Pooter is the hero of the comic novel The Diary of a ..., a man of no importance
a wine taster dismissing a thin wine might say it has ...

explanation.walkthrough: Pooter is the self-important clerk of the Grossmiths' Victorian comic novel The Diary of a Nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooter is the fictional insignificant person whose diary gives the novel its title.

clue.text: Preparing to have year in university

indicators.note: in tells you the letter for year is placed within the university's name

parts.note: Reading is an English town with a university

explanation.surface: A student is getting ready to spend a year at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts Y inside READING, a university town west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Readying something means making it fit for use, getting it set up.

clue.text: Noble chaps, these aggressive strikers?

definitions.meaning: the highest rank of British nobleman below a prince
... is old slang for fists, as in 'put up your ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Dukes are peers of top rank, and in boxing slang the word also means the fists.

clue.text: Little man's short flight in place of uncle

parts.note: a pawn is the smallest piece in chess, a chessman
the 's of man's supplies an S
a hop is a short flight, as in a quick plane trip

explanation.surface: A small man takes a brief flight to visit a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle is slang for a pawnbroker, whose shop lends money on pledged goods.

clue.text: Drink cartel diversifying

indicators.note: diversifying means varying, so the word cartel has its letters varied

explanation.surface: A drinks cartel branches out into new products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversifying' rearranges CARTEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.

clue.text: North American wood left out becomes dark brown

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is taken away from the timber word

parts.note: lumber is the North American word for timber

explanation.surface: Timber in America, with some left out, turns a deep brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' removes L from LUMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a natural earth pigment giving a dark brownish colour.

clue.text: Refuse to accept delivery by jet

parts.note: jet black, so jet means black
in cricket a ball is one delivery by the bowler

explanation.surface: A fast bowler's ball is rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket each delivery is a ball; jet is a deep black.
explanation.definitionFit: To blackball is to vote against admitting someone, from the black balls once dropped in a ballot box.

clue.text: By staying on the outside, not so much led astray, fortunately

indicators.note: the two letters of the first word remain around the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
not so much means less

indicators.note: astray means gone wrong, so the letters of led are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is lucky to stay on the fringes and be led astray less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' gives DEL, the anagram of the printed 'led'; 'staying on the outside' keeps the first word of the clue wrapped round everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Blessedly means luckily, by a happy chance, as if by heaven's favour.

clue.text: Fly without new navigation aid

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the flying word goes round the letter for new

parts.note: to fly is to soar

explanation.surface: A pilot flies without a fresh navigation system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside: SOAR goes around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar locates objects underwater by echoes, guiding ships and submarines.

clue.text: Synthetic polymer trimmed for use

indicators.note: synthetic means made up artificially, so the letters are recombined
trimmed means the word polymer loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A man-made plastic is cut down to be put to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed' cuts POLYMER to POLYME, and 'Synthetic' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Employ as a noun means service or use, as in being in someone's employ.

clue.text: Sailor's left noisy party in Mediterranean harbour

parts.note: port is the nautical term for the left-hand side of a ship

indicators.note: noisy says the word for party is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute or game

explanation.surface: A sailor leaves a rowdy party at a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisy' turns SIDE into its sound-alike SAID, giving the Egyptian port at the north end of the Suez Canal.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Said is the Egyptian city where the Suez Canal meets the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Picture of biscuits just out of the oven?

parts.note: ginger snaps are crisp biscuits
freshly baked food is hot

explanation.surface: A photograph of freshly baked cookies.
explanation.walkthrough: Snaps are thin crisp biscuits, as in brandy snaps or ginger snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quickly taken informal photograph.

clue.text: Fit flap in fashionable suit this person is bringing

indicators.note: fashionable is read as able to be fashioned, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A tailor fits a flap into a smart suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' rearranges FIT FLAP IN. The 'suit' is a lawsuit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who brings a legal action against someone in court.

clue.text: Bound to get cramp

definitions.meaning: to bound is to set limits to something
to cramp is to hamper or confine

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to confine within limits, checking freedom of movement.

clue.text: Haggled like the composer's wife?

definitions.meaning: Smetana's opera The ... Bride, whose bride was traded

explanation.walkthrough: The composer is Smetana, whose comic opera is The Bartered Bride.
explanation.definitionFit: To haggle is to bargain over terms, and bargaining by exchanging goods is trading.

clue.text: Pronounced rupture in lower dorsal area

indicators.note: pronounced tells you the word for rupture is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a rupture is a breach

explanation.surface: A doctor notes a marked tear in the lower back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' turns BREACH into its sound-alike, and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The breech is the buttocks, as in a breech birth where the baby comes bottom first.

clue.text: Hold up basket of food

definitions.meaning: to hold up is to hinder or impede
a wicker container of provisions, as for a picnic

explanation.definitionFit: To hinder progress is to obstruct, and a picnic box of wicker is the noun sense.

clue.text: Book store

definitions.meaning: to book is to arrange in advance, as with a table
a store is a supply kept back for later

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to secure a place ahead of time; the other is a stock held back for later.

clue.text: One used to stiff examinations nonetheless is in an awkward position

indicators.note: read as none less: a nought, the letter O, is subtracted

parts.note: a coroner investigates deaths, so examining stiffs (corpses) is routine

explanation.surface: A cool-headed examiner still finds himself in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' is read as 'no one less' or 'none less': drop an O (nought) from CORONER. A stiff is slang for a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner is a tight spot from which escape is difficult, as in being backed into one.

clue.text: Guarantee, when queen is removed, to succeed

indicators.note: is removed tells you the letter for queen comes out of the guarantee word

parts.note: to guarantee is to ensure
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A promise is void once the queen is gone, so another must succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is removed' takes R (Regina) out of ENSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on afterwards, coming next in sequence.

clue.text: Resin — one seen after Oriental cuts tree

indicators.note: seen after places the letter for one at the end
cuts means the Oriental letter slices into the tree's name

parts.note: an elm is a tree
E, for east, stands for Oriental
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man from the East cuts a tree and resin is seen to ooze out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' puts E inside ELM; 'seen after' then adds I.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant gum from tropical trees, used in varnishes and ointments.

clue.text: Unlike Herrick's rose, lacking old-fashioned character

parts.note: thorn is an Old English letter, a runic character for th
lacking means without, -less

explanation.surface: Unlike the poet's rose, someone is short of an old-style personality.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Herrick wrote of the rose with thorns ('The Rose'): the answer is its opposite. The thorn is an obsolete letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose of the poet's verse has prickles; the answer describes one without any.

clue.text: Unusually wide, perhaps

definitions.meaning: ... as an adverb means exceptionally, as in ... large
in cricket a wide is a run added to the score that the batsman did not hit

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a wide (a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach) is one kind of these bonus runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide is one type of run credited to the batting side without a stroke; the adverb sense means especially.

clue.text: Standard formal procedure half repeated in study

indicators.note: in places the procedure and its repeated half inside the study word

parts.note: to con is to study
a rite is a formal ceremony or procedure

indicators.note: half repeated means the first half of that procedure word comes again

parts.note: a rite is a formal ceremony or procedure

explanation.surface: A standard ceremonial procedure is half repeated during study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half repeated' gives RI, the first half of the procedure word, said a second time; 'in' puts the whole run inside the word for study.
explanation.definitionFit: A criterion is a standard by which something is judged.

clue.text: Put underground in wintertime

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie within the word wintertime

explanation.surface: Something is buried in the winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' tells you the answer sits inside WINTERTIME.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body in a grave.

clue.text: Oil container, perhaps

parts.note: an oil is read as an oil painting, and the container is what surrounds it on the wall

explanation.definitionFit: An oil painting is mounted in a border of wood or gilt that holds and displays it.
